results.reason: R148 clause 4.2 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this M1 rear lamp contains. The clause applies the pertinent R48 sections 5 and 6 and their Annexes, where they can be checked at lamp type approval. The candidate keeps that condition. The wording "and the vehicle category" matches the clause's reference to the category the lamp is installed on.

Clause 4.3 requires lamps to keep working satisfactorily and keep the prescribed characteristics in normal use despite vibration. The product is a vehicle lamp with R148-scope functions (position, stop, reversing), so the clause applies. The candidate wording matches the clause.
R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which are the rear lamp's functions. Clause 3.3.3.1 requires lamps to bear the approval marking, and the candidate states this without change.
The rear lamp is a lamp within R148 scope. Clause 3.3.3.2 requires the applicant's trade name or mark, and the candidate matches it.
The lamp must carry an approval marking. Clause 3.3.4.1 sets where it goes, and the candidate wording matches the clause.

The rear lamp is fitted on an M1 vehicle, so clause 3.3.4.2 applies. The candidate keeps the "if any" condition for LED substitute light source categories, and the spec does not say whether the product has such a category.

R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which are the product's lamp functions. Para 3.3.2.1 requires the approval mark: a circle around "E" followed by the country's distinguishing number. The candidate keeps that wording.
The rear position lamp is within R148 scope. Para 3.3.2.2 requires the four to six-digit sequential number from the approval number, placed close to the approval mark. The candidate matches this.

The product has position, stop and reversing lamps, all R148 lamps. Para 3.3.2.3 requires the symbols that identify the lamp functions under para 3.2.4. The candidate reflects this. I did not read para 3.2.4 itself.
The lamps fall under R148. Para 3.3.2.4 requires the regulation number, the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at approval. The candidate matches this.

R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the product combines. Paragraph 3.5 requires conformity of production to 1958 Agreement Schedule 1 and the requirements of paragraph 6, and the candidate keeps both. The spec does not say the lamp is approved, so applying 3.5 assumes the lamp is type-approved under R148.

Paragraph 3.7 obliges the approval holder to inform the granting authority when it completely ceases to manufacture an approved lamp. The product falls within R148 lamp types, and the candidate keeps the condition of complete cessation. The spec does not state that an approval exists, so the holder's obligation depends on the lamp being approved.

Paragraph 4.1 requires each lamp submitted for approval to conform to paragraphs 4 and 5. The product's position, stop and reversing functions are within the R148 scope in paragraph 1, and the candidate restates the clause accurately.

The rear lamp combines position, stop and reversing lamps, which are in R148 scope. It uses LED electronics. Clause 4.7.2.3 sets the EMC disturbance limit for light signalling devices. The candidate omits the footnote that EMC compliance is relevant to the vehicle type. That omission does not change the obligation.

Clause 4.8.1 requires all photometric and colorimetric measurements to follow the stated conditions, with method particulars in Annex 3. The product's position, stop and reversing functions fall under these measurements. The candidate's wording matches the clause.

Clause 4.8.1.2 applies to lamps with light source modules or non-replaceable light sources. The product has LED modules on a PCB built into the lamp, so this condition fits. The spec does not say whether the LEDs are replaceable, but the clause covers both modules and non-replaceable sources.
Clause 4.8.1.4 is a general photometric test condition that requires masking against stray reflections. It applies to the lamp's photometric measurements. The candidate repeats the clause accurately.
UN R148 paragraph 1 lists position, stop and reversing lamps in its scope. The product integrates all three functions, so the scope applies.

Paragraph 3.1.1 says the type approval application is submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by his duly accredited representative. The product's lamp functions fall under UN R148, so the rule applies. The candidate wording matches the clause.

Paragraph 3.1.2 says the application must be accompanied by the listed documents, starting with the drawings in 3.1.2.1. The rear lamp needs type approval under UN R148, so this applies. The candidate wording is general but faithful to the clause.

Paragraph 3.1.2.2 requires a brief technical description stating in particular the listed items. The candidate keeps the conditional items (rear window optics only if mounted inside the vehicle, logo statement only where applicable). The spec does not say whether the light sources are replaceable, so the replaceable-source items are conditional. The candidate's phrase 'These include' does not make them mandatory.

R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the product combines. Paragraph 3.3.4.5 requires the approval marking, and any applicable listed markings, to be on the lamp. The candidate keeps the "applicable" qualifier.

The product is a combined multi-function lamp that includes a retro-reflector, so it plausibly complies with several UN Regulations. Paragraph 3.3.5.1 permits a single approval mark. The candidate keeps it optional and keeps the conditions that follow it.
Paragraph 3.3.5.1.1 requires a single approval mark on combined lamps to be visible after installation. The candidate keeps the condition that it applies only if a single mark is used.

Paragraph 3.3.5.1.2 says no light-transmitting part can be removed without also removing the approval mark. The product has an outer lens and a retro-reflector that transmit light. The candidate keeps the condition that it applies only if a single mark is used.

Paragraph 3.3.5.2 sets a minimum size for the components of a single approval mark, based on the smallest individual mark. It applies to the combined lamp if a single mark is used, and the candidate preserves that.

Paragraph 3.4.1 requires every modification of a lamp type to be notified to the approving Type Approval Authority. The product is a lamp type within R148 scope. The cited spec quote is weak evidence, but the product is clearly covered lamp types.

R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this rear lamp contains. The spec lists "LED modules on PCB" in plural, so the lamp plausibly has several light sources. The candidate keeps the condition that the group is wired so failure of one stops all of them, and only then deems it one light source. The spec does not give the wiring, so this is a conditional rule.

4.6.1.2 applies to a single lamp with more than one light source. The multi-LED rear lamp plausibly meets that condition, though the spec gives no source count. The candidate keeps both alternatives: (a) the Annex 3 minimum intensity is still met and the maximum is not exceeded with all sources lit, or (b) a failure tell-tale is produced, with the communication-form note.

4.7.1 applies to the lamps in R148's scope. The product's LED modules on a PCB must be one of the permitted types: an approved replaceable source, a light source module, or a non-replaceable source. The candidate preserves the condition that no use restriction is declared at application for the replaceable sources.

R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this product includes. Paragraph 3.1.2.7(a) requires two complete samples 'if not otherwise specified' and allows identical samples for symmetrical left and right lamps. The candidate keeps both conditions. It leaves out 3.1.2.7(b) on variable-intensity lamps, which does not apply here.
Paragraph 3.2.1 requires a separate approval for each lamp listed in paragraph 1. The scope lists position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three, so the clause applies.

Paragraph 3.2.2 covers units of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps. The product combines several lamp functions in one housing. The candidate preserves the rule that each lamp must satisfy R148 or another Regulation. The retro-reflector is not a lamp, so it falls outside this clause.

Paragraph 3.2.3 says approval is granted if the submitted lamp type meets R148, and that all devices of an interdependent system must be submitted by the same applicant. The candidate reframes the first part as an obligation on the applicant. It keeps the interdependence condition as conditional, which suits a spec that does not say whether the system is interdependent.

The product has a reversing lamp, which is within R148 scope (paragraph 5.8, category AR). Paragraph 5.8.1 requires each of the two samples to meet Table 10. It allows verification only up to 30° inwards, at a minimum of 2.5·10^1 cd (25 cd), for lamps installed exclusively as a pair. It requires that condition to be stated in the application documents and in paragraph 9.1.3 of the communication form. The candidate preserves all of this.

Table 10 for category AR gives a minimum of 80 cd and maximums of 300 cd in or above the h-plane, 600 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D, and 8000 cd below 5°D. It specifies the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V. The candidate matches these values and applies to the product's reversing lamp.
R148 4.8.1.7 applies to the position, stop and reversing lamps, which are in R148's scope. The candidate keeps the 'if not otherwise specified' condition. The LED light source is consistent with it.
4.8.1.8 sets the conditional measurement requirements used if results are challenged. The candidate correctly points to 4.8.1.8.1–4.8.1.8.3 and applies to the product's photometric testing.

4.8.1.8.1 requires a measurement distance at which the inverse-square law applies, and the candidate keeps the 'if challenged' condition. It is relevant to photometry of the stop lamp and the other lamps.
4.8.1.8.2 matches the candidate: receiver angular aperture between 10' and 1 degree, seen from the reference centre, applied when results are challenged.
4.8.1.8.3 matches the candidate: a requirement is deemed met if it is met within a quarter degree of the direction of observation, applied when results are challenged.

4.8.1.9 requires the limits of the apparent surface to be determined along the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp. The product's position, stop and reversing lamps fall under it. The clause's exceptions (category 5 and 6 direction indicators, rear-registration plate lamps) are not relevant to this product.

4.8.2 sets the test supply voltages of 6.75 V, 13.5 V or 28 V by system voltage, unless otherwise specified. The candidate keeps all three options and the 'unless otherwise specified' condition. The spec does not state the system voltage, but the candidate does not assume one.
UN R148 covers stop lamps (scope, para 5.5). The product has a stop lamp. Para 5.5.1 requires each of the two samples supplied to meet Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution.

Table 7 gives minimum and maximum intensities, standard light distribution and geometric visibility minimums by stop lamp category (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS). Maximums are lower for lamps marked "D". The candidate keeps the "for its category" condition. The spec does not state the category, but the candidate does not assume one.
Para 5.5.2 requires the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility, by reference to Table 7. The product has a stop lamp, so this applies.

The product is a multi-function rear lamp with R148 functions: rear position, stop and reversing. Paragraph 3.2.3.2 requires an approval number for each approved lamp type and bars reusing it for another lamp type of the same function. The candidate keeps that limit.
Paragraph 3.2.4 covers the symbols identifying each approved lamp function. The product has several R148 functions. The clause text is truncated, so this relies on the lead-in to Table 1.

Table 1 gives symbols for the rear position lamp (R1/R2), stop lamp (S1/S2) and reversing lamp (AR), which match the product's functions. The steady or variable wording follows the table's variants. The spec does not say which variant applies.
Paragraph 3.2.5 requires the change index for each device to follow the series of amendments, and the product's lamp functions are devices covered by that rule.
Table 2 gives change indexes of 0 (series 00) or 1 (series 01) for rear position, stop and reversing lamps. These match the product's functions.

Paragraph 3.3.1.1 requires every device of an approved type to have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings. It applies to this lamp, whose housing and lens can carry them.
Paragraph 3.3.1.1.1 requires all markings to be clearly legible and indelible. It applies to the approved lamp's markings.
Paragraph 3.3.1.2 sets the approval marking dimension 'a' at no less than 5 mm. The candidate states this accurately, and it applies to an approved R148 lamp.

Paragraph 5.2.1 applies to rear position lamps, and the product has one. The candidate keeps the two-sample Table 4 requirement. It also keeps the 60 cd allowance below 5° for lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps. The spec shows a combined housing with both functions, so this allowance may apply, though it is conditional.

Table 4 gives the rear position lamp limits: R1 4–17 cd (8.5 cd if marked D), R2 4–42 cd (21 cd if marked D), Figure A3-I, and 0.05 cd minimum in the geometric visibility angles. The candidate states these correctly and ties them to the lamp's category. The spec does not name the category, so the candidate lists both.
Paragraph 5.2.2 refers to Table 4, which sets a 0.05 cd minimum within the angles of geometric visibility. This applies to the product's rear position lamp.
Paragraph 5.2.7 requires red light from rear position lamps. The product has a rear position lamp and a red-tinted lens, which is consistent with this.

R148 scope covers stop lamps, and the product has a stop lamp. Clause 5.5.6 sends stop lamps to the failure provisions in 4.6, which the candidate states. I did not read the full text of 4.6. The search snippets show it covers failure of light sources in lamps, and other lamp types point to it in the same way.
Clause 5.5.7 sits under 5.5 Stop lamps and says the colour of light emitted shall be red. The product has a stop lamp and a red-tinted lens, so the candidate matches the clause.

results.reason: R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the product includes. Paragraph 6.1 requires lamps to be manufactured to conform to the approved type, with paragraph 5 compliance verified. The candidate cites only 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 and leaves out 6.1.3, the 20% deviation limit. That is a minor incompleteness, not a contradiction.

Paragraph 6.1.1 requires compliance with the minimum conformity-of-production control procedures in Annex 4. The product's position, stop and reversing lamps fall within R148 scope. The wording matches the clause.
Paragraph 6.1.2 requires compliance with the minimum sampling-by-inspector requirements in Annex 5. The product's lamps fall within R148 scope. The wording matches the clause.

R148 4.8.2.4 applies to the position, stop and reversing lamp functions in this rear lamp. The candidate keeps the conditions: control gear or variable intensity control only 'if applicable', and the voltage with tolerances is noted in the Annex 1 communication form. The spec doesn't mention control gear, but the candidate's 'where applicable' wording covers that.

4.8.3.1(a) requires the minimum intensity on the HV axis from the paragraph 5 table. This applies to the rear position lamp function. The candidate leaves out 'if not otherwise specified', which is a minor omission.
4.8.3.1(b) sets a maximum intensity in any direction where the lamp is visible, taken from the paragraph 5 table. This applies to the stop lamp function.

The candidate combines 4.8.3.1(c) and (d): the minimum within the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles, the Annex 3 distribution outside the reference axis, and the Annex 3 local-variation provisions. All of these apply to the lamp's light functions, including reversing.
4.8.3.6 requires luminous intensity compliance tests to follow Annex 8. This applies to the lamp's stop, position and reversing functions.

4.9 requires colour to be measured inside the Annex 3 grid field using the 4.8 procedure, with no sharp colour variation outside it. Lamps with non-replaceable light sources are checked with the sources in place. The candidate keeps this condition. The spec's LED modules on PCB are plausibly non-replaceable, but the spec doesn't say so.

R148 scope (clause 1) covers stop, position and reversing lamps, and the product spec lists all three functions. Annex 1 is the communication form for approving a lamp type under R148. It has fields for the lamp function(s), the category and the approval number, so the proposed obligation matches it. The form is issued by the approving Administration, not the manufacturer. I did not read the approval-provisions clause that references Annex 1, so confidence is moderate.

R148 scope (clause 1) covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this product has. Annex 1 item 5 of the communication form asks for the date submitted for approval. The candidate wording matches that item.
The product's stop lamp is within R148 scope. Annex 1 item 6 of the communication form identifies the Technical Service responsible for the approval tests. The candidate wording matches that item.
The product's lamps are within R148 scope. Annex 1 item 7 of the communication form gives the date of the Technical Service's report. The candidate wording matches that item.
The product's lamps are within R148 scope. Annex 1 item 8 of the communication form gives the number of the Technical Service's report. The candidate wording matches that item.

The product includes a reversing lamp, and Annex 1 item 9.1.3 applies to a reversing lamp. It asks whether the lamp is to be installed only as part of a pair (yes/no). The candidate keeps that condition.

UN R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this rear lamp includes. Annex 1 item 9.2 asks for particulars by light signalling function. These include colour, number, category and kind of light source, light source module, control gear and mounting conditions. The spec lists LED modules on PCB. The candidate's "other particulars" wording is acceptable because the clause itself marks some items as conditional.

Annex 1 item 9.3 names the rear position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. The clause asks for a yes/no declaration on use only with a vehicle fitted with a failure tell-tale. The candidate states this correctly.
Annex 1 item 10 requires the position of the approval mark to be given in the communication. The rear lamp is a UN R148 lamp type, so this item applies. The candidate matches the clause.
R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this M1 rear lamp contains. Annex 4 para 1.1 on mechanical and geometric conformity matches the candidate wording.
The stop, position and reversing functions are R148 lamps. Annex 4 para 1.2 on photometric conformity of randomly chosen lamps, tested per para 4.8, is accurately restated.
The red lens defines the signal colour of the R148 lamp functions. Annex 4 para 1.3 requires chromaticity coordinates to be met when tested under para 4.9, and the candidate keeps that condition.

Annex 4 para 2 requires the type approval holder to run minimum tests at appropriate intervals and, if sampling shows non-conformity, to take further samples and act. This applies to the R148 lamp types in the product, and the wording matches.
Annex 4 para 2.1 says conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics. This applies to the coloured lamp functions of the product.

Table A2-1 row "Front/rear position (A, R1, R2)" gives 45°/80°, with (20°/80°) only below the H-plane for H-plane height under 750 mm. It gives vertical 15°/15°, with (15°/5°) for height under 750 mm. The candidate matches these and keeps the limits. It omits the optional (5°/15°) value for lamps above 2,100 mm, which is not relevant to an M1 rear position lamp. The product has a rear position lamp on an M1 vehicle, and the R1/R2 row is the one that applies to M1.

Table A2-1 row "Stop lamp (S1, S2)" gives 45°/45°, with (20°/45°) only below the H-plane for H-plane height under 750 mm. It gives vertical 15°/15°, with (15°/5°) for height under 750 mm. The candidate matches these and keeps the limits. It omits the optional (5°/15°) value for lamps above 2,100 mm, which is not relevant to an M1 stop lamp. The product has a stop lamp on an M1 vehicle, and the S1/S2 row is the one that applies to M1.

Annex 3 §1.1 applies to the product's rear position and stop lamps. The candidate keeps the condition that the 5°-downward limit applies only to lamps with H plane at or below 750 mm, and only to S1/S2 stop lamps. The stop lamp category and mounting height are not stated in the spec, but the wording is conditional, so this does not undermine the match.
Annex 3 §1.2 sets the substantial-uniformity rule for the grid light distribution. It covers the product's position and stop lamps, and the candidate states it accurately.
The reversing-lamp exception in §1.2 applies because the product has a reversing lamp. The 50% check is stated with its visual-examination condition intact.

Annex 3 §2.1 gives the standard light distribution for rear position lamps and S1/S2/MS stop lamps, as percentages of the minimum intensities in the relevant tables. The product has rear position and stop lamps. The stop lamp category is not given, but the candidate limits the stop-lamp part to S1/S2.

Annex 8 / 2.1.5 applies to any lamp (function) and keeps the "in case of doubt" condition. The candidate keeps that condition. Position, stop and reversing lamps are all within R148 scope and are listed in Table A8-1. The spec says the light source is LED modules on PCB, so under 2.1.2 the lamp is normally deemed compliant at all times. The 2.1.5 doubt-based extended test is therefore only a conditional obligation. The candidate's stated reason, that the functions "fall under the Table A8-1 run-up regime", is imprecise. The spec does not say the lamp is LED-only.

results.reason: R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this rear lamp contains. Annex 4 para 2.2.1 requires conformity tests to follow the R148 methods, and the candidate says the same.

Para 2.2.2 allows the manufacturer to use equivalent methods with the competent authority's consent and puts the burden of proving equivalence on the manufacturer. The candidate keeps both conditions. The lamp is an R148 device.
Para 2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and its correlation with the competent authority's measurements. This applies to the lamp's conformity testing.
Para 2.2.4 makes the R148 methods the reference methods in all cases, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches this.

Para 2.3 requires random sampling from a uniform batch of one type. It lets a manufacturer group records from several factories only if they share the same quality system and management. The candidate is faithful to this and the lamp is a series-produced R148 lamp.
Para 2.4 requires photometric measurement at the Annex 3 points and checking of the chromaticity coordinates. This applies to the stop, position and reversing functions of the lamp.

Para 2.5 makes the manufacturer responsible for a statistical study and for acceptability criteria agreed with the authority. The criteria must give a minimum 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 5 spot check at 95% confidence. The candidate reproduces this.
Annex 5 para 1.1 treats mechanical and geometric conformity as satisfied when differences stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations. This applies to a mass-produced R148 lamp.

Annex 5 para 1.2(a) says conformity is not contested if no measured value deviates from the para 6.1.3 values. The candidate states this in a slightly stronger form. Sub-item (b), on replaceable light sources, does not matter here because the product uses LED modules.

Annex 5 para 1.4 requires the chromaticity coordinates to comply when tested under para 4.9. The product's position, stop and reversing lamps are within R148 scope (para 1), and the outer lens sets the colour.
Annex 5 para 2 selects four lamps at random and marks them A and B. R148 covers the product's position, stop and reversing lamps, so the CoP sampling applies.

Annex 5 para 2.1 says conformity is not contested if every specimen in A and B deviates by no more than 20%. It also allows measurement to stop if both lamps of A deviate by no more than 0%. The candidate keeps both conditions.

Annex 5 para 2.2 contests conformity if any specimen of A or B deviates by more than 20%. The manufacturer must then align production, and repeat sampling follows within two months of notification. The candidate matches this. It leaves out only the retention of samples A and B, which does not change the obligation.
Annex 5 para 3 selects four lamps at random from stock made after alignment and marks them C and D. This applies to the R148 lamp product.
Annex 5 para 3.1 matches the candidate. It gives the 20% limit for samples C and D and the 0% early-termination condition for sample C.
Annex 5 para 3.2.1 covers deviations above 20% but not above 30%. In that case the manufacturer must align again, and a second repeated sampling follows within two months. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 para 3.2.2 withdraws approval and applies para 5 if one specimen of C or D deviates by more than 30%. The candidate matches this and applies to a type-approved R148 lamp.
Annex 5 para 4 selects four lamps at random from stock made after alignment and marks them E and F. This applies to the R148 lamp product.
Annex 5 para 4.1 matches the candidate. It gives the 20% limit for samples E and F and the 0% early-termination condition for sample E.

Annex 8 para 1.2.1 covers reversing lamps that use non-incandescent technology. The product has a reversing lamp with LED modules. The candidate keeps the 1 min and 10 min intensity requirement and the option to calculate from the photometric-stability distribution using HV ratios.

Para 1.2.2 covers all non-incandescent lamps other than reversing and manoeuvring lamps. That includes the LED rear position and stop lamps. The candidate keeps the 1 min check plus either 30 min or photometric stability. It omits the optional calculation and the direction-indicator sentence, which do not apply here.

Para 2.1 applies the additional Table A8-1 checks only 'depending on the light source technology'. Para 2.1.2 says an LED-only lamp is deemed to comply at all points in time if the para 1.2 measurements comply. The product uses LED modules, so no separate additional check is required. The candidate drops this condition and states an unconditional extra obligation.

Table A8-1 lists the times (position 4 s, stop 0.2 s, reversing 0.2 s) for additional checks that depend on light source technology. For an LED-only lamp, para 2.1.2 deems compliance if the para 1.2 values comply. The candidate presents the additional checks as required for this LED product, which contradicts that. The spec does not show any other light source technology.

The clause sets the geometry limits δ≤10', γ≤10' and η≤80' for measuring retro-reflective devices. The candidate reproduces them and they apply to the retro-reflector.
The clause says stray reflections "should" be avoided by masking during photometric measurements. The candidate keeps this as a recommendation, and it applies to testing the retro-reflector.

R150 covers retro-reflectors, and the spec lists a retro-reflector as a main part of the lamp. Clause 3.6 requires a measuring distance that respects the angle limits and is at least 10 m, and the candidate keeps both conditions.

Clause 3.7 sets the illuminance uniformity condition for the retro-reflective device. It specifies a measuring element of at most one-tenth of the examined area and max/min ≤ 1.05. The candidate matches this, and the spec's retro-reflector falls within R150.

Clause 3.8.1 requires the photometer head to be corrected to the CIE photopic spectral luminous efficiency. This is a test-equipment requirement for photometry of the product's retro-reflector, and the candidate states it accurately.

Clause 3.8.2 requires no perceptible change in local sensitivity across the photometer aperture, otherwise suitable provisions such as a diffusing window. The candidate keeps this condition and applies to retro-reflector photometry.

Clause 4.1.1 calls for minimising stray light. It says the field of view and light spread shall be restricted as much as possible, and the background and holder should be matt black. The candidate reflects this and applies to retro-reflector photometry.
Clause 4.1.2 requires floor and wall reflections to be screened from the sample and the photometer head by baffles. The candidate matches this, and it applies to testing the retro-reflector.
Clause 4.1.3 provides for measuring residual stray light with the sample covered by a black surface and subtracting it from the retro-reflector measurement. The candidate paraphrases this adequately.

Clause 4.2.1 recommends ('should') a stable source and photometer head, limited ambient temperature variation, and stabilisation time before measurement. The candidate keeps the recommended wording, and it applies to retro-reflector photometry.

Annex 6 Part 1 para 1 covers moulded plastics reflectors of Class IA and IB retro-reflecting devices. The product has a moulded PMMA prism retro-reflector. The spec does not name the class. A rear retro-reflector on an M1 is normally Class IA or IB, and both fall inside the clause's list. The 48 h, 65 ±2 °C dry soak and the 1 h cool-down at 23 ±2 °C match the clause.

Annex 6 Part 1 para 3 requires that no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, especially its optical component, be visible after the heat test. The product has an integrated retro-reflector, so this applies.

Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1 applies to retro-reflective devices "whether part of a lamp or not", which covers the integrated retro-reflector. The candidate keeps the key parameters: 10 min at 50 ±5 °C, 20 mm below the surface, repeat turned 180°, then immersion at 25 ±5 °C.

Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.2 says no water may reach the reflecting surface of the optical unit. Clearly visible water means the device fails. This matches the candidate and applies to the product's retro-reflector.
Annex 5 para 2.4 requires photometric measurements at the specified points and chromaticity coordinates on the sampled device. The product includes a retro-reflector.
Para 2.5 puts the statistical study and acceptability criteria, agreed with the Type Approval Authority, on the manufacturer. The 95% confidence and 0.95 pass probability match the clause.
Para 1.2.1 sets the 20% unfavourable deviation limit from the prescribed minimum values for a randomly chosen device. It applies to the retro-reflector.
Para 1.3 says the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with. It applies to the retro-reflector.

Paras 2 and 2.2 cover the first sampling of four devices in samples A and B. Conformity is contested if any specimen exceeds 20%. The manufacturer must then align production, and repeated sampling follows.
Para 3.1 says conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 20%. The candidate's 'after alignment' framing matches para 3.
Para 3.2.1 covers a specimen of C or D over 20% with none over 30%. The manufacturer must align again, and a second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification.
Para 3.2.2 says approval is withdrawn if a specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30%.
Para 4.1 says conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples E and F deviates by more than 20%.
Para 4.2 says conformity is contested if a specimen of E or F exceeds 20%. Approval is then withdrawn under para 5, which refers to para 3.6.

Para 6.1 requires one retro-reflector of sample A to pass the Annex 6 Part 2 water-penetration test. If it fails, both devices of sample B are tested and both must pass. The Advance Warning Triangle variant does not apply to this product.
Annex 5 Part 1 para 1.1 gives the mirror-effect check when measuring RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, with a reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° if there is an effect. It applies to the retro-reflector.

Clause 2.2.6 is a real source for the proposed wording. It says RI is measured per Part 1 of Annex 4 after the exterior is dried with a dry cotton cloth. But it sits in Annex 6 Part 3, an alternative moisture and dust test. That test applies only to Class IB and IIIB retro-reflectors, which are combined with signal lamps that are not watertight. It applies only if the manufacturer requests it, and only after the water spray and drain steps. The spec shows a retro-reflector combined in one housing with the rear lamp functions. It does not give the retro-reflector class, say whether the housing is watertight, or say the alternative test was chosen. The candidate also leaves out these conditions. Applicability therefore can't be confirmed.

UN R150 covers retro-reflectors, and the product has a PMMA prism retro-reflector in its rear lamp. Annex 6 Part 4 para 1 requires retained photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite humidity and corrosion. It requires checks of front-surface tarnishing and rear-face protection, especially where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked. It points to ISO 9227:2017 for the corrosion test description. The candidate keeps these conditions.

Annex 6 Part 4 para 2 says that where the retro-reflector is combined with a light, the lamp is stripped of removable parts and exposed to saline mist for 50 hours. That is two 24-hour exposures with a 2-hour drying interval. The product's retro-reflector shares a single housing with the lamp functions, so the combined-lamp condition is met. The candidate matches the clause text.

Annex 7 Part 2 para 1.1 requires the outer and illuminating surface of a moulded plastics retro-reflector to be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. The surface is cleaned after about 5 minutes. The product has a moulded PMMA prism retro-reflector. The clause covers the retro-reflector classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, and a rear retro-reflector on an M1 car should fall in one of them. The spec does not state the class, so this is a mild inference.

The same para 1.1 requires RI to be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 after the oil exposure and cleaning. This applies to the product's moulded plastics retro-reflector in the same way as the wiping step. The spec does not state the retro-reflector class.

R23 covers reversing lamps on M-category vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a reversing lamp. Paragraph 2.1 requires the holder of the trade name or mark, or an accredited representative, to submit the application. It also makes the installation-inclination statement optional, at the applicant's choice. The candidate keeps both points.
Paragraph 2.2 requires each reversing lamp type's application to be accompanied by the listed documents and samples. The product's reversing lamp falls under it.

Paragraph 2.2.1 requires triplicate drawings showing the mounting position, reference axis, reference centre and approval mark position. The candidate correctly limits the mounting height and orientation requirement to manoeuvring lamps. The product's reversing lamp is in scope.

Paragraph 2.2.2 requires a technical description stating the filament lamp category, LED light source category or light source module code. It excepts lamps with non-replaceable light sources, and the candidate keeps that exception. The product uses LED modules. The spec does not say whether they are replaceable, so the exception stays conditional, which the candidate preserves.
Paragraph 2.2.3 requires two samples. It allows identical samples when the devices are symmetrical left/right, and the candidate keeps that allowance. The product's reversing lamp is in scope.

Annex 6 Part 3 is an alternative moisture and dust test. It applies only to Class IB and IIIB retro-reflectors, and only at the manufacturer's request. The spec shows a retro-reflector combined with signal lamps in one housing. It does not give the R150 class or say whether the lamp is watertight, and it does not say the alternative test is elected. The candidate text leaves out these conditions.

The nozzle requirement belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class, watertightness, or any election of the alternative. The candidate text omits these conditions.
The 45° ± 5° nozzle angle is part of the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.

The platform requirement belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected, and the candidate omits that condition.
The precipitation rate belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.
The sample procedure belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class (IB or another) or say whether the alternative is elected.

The clause applies only inside the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec also does not say whether the lamp has drain holes or openings. Applicability to this product cannot be confirmed.
The rotation speed belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.

The product does group signalling functions with a retro-reflector, which fits the clause's condition. However, the clause sits within the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.
The 12-hour duration belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.
The drain period belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected.

The moisture evaluation belongs to the optional Part 3 alternative for Class IB and IIIB devices. The spec does not give the class or say whether the alternative is elected. The candidate also leaves out the RI measurement that the clause requires.
Para 3.1 requires lamps submitted for approval to bear the applicant's trade name or mark, legible and indelible. The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers.
Para 3.4 requires adequate space for the approval mark and the para 4.3 additional symbols, shown in the 2.2.1 drawing. This applies to the reversing lamp function.

Para 3.5 applies only to lamps with non-replaceable light sources or light source module(s). The spec says only 'LED modules on PCB' and does not say whether the sources are non-replaceable or are R23 light source modules, so the condition is not established.

Para 4.1 says approval 'shall be granted' if the two samples meet the requirements. That is a duty of the approval authority, not a product requirement. The candidate also turns it into 'only if', which the clause does not say.

Para 4.3 and 4.3.1 require an approved reversing lamp to bear, in the para 3.4 space, an international approval mark (circle around E plus country number) and an approval number. This fits the reversing lamp function.
Para 4.3.2 requires the additional symbol of letters A and R, as shown in Annex 2, on reversing lamps. The product includes a reversing lamp.
The product has a reversing lamp, and R23 6.1.1 sets minimum and maximum intensities for reversing lamps. The candidate keeps the "two samples" and axis-of-reference conditions.
R23 6.1.2 requires at least 80 cd along the axis of reference for a reversing lamp. The product has a reversing lamp, and the candidate states the value correctly.

R23 6.1.3 sets maximum intensities of 300 cd at or above the horizontal, 600 cd between h-h and 5° D, and 8,000 cd below 5° D. The candidate reproduces these correctly for the product's reversing lamp.

R23 6.1.4 requires the Annex 3 minima in every other direction. It allows verification only up to 30° inwards, with at least 25 cd, for lamps installed exclusively as a pair. The candidate keeps the declaration conditions. The product's reversing lamp falls within scope.

R150 covers retro-reflectors. Annex 6 Part 4 para 2 applies the corrosion test to the device, or to the lamp if the device is combined with a light. Para 4.1 sets the post-test requirement of no excessive corrosion liable to impair efficiency. The product is a rear lamp with an integrated retro-reflector, so this applies. Para 5.1.6 lets approval authorities omit unnecessary tests depending on materials. That is a possible exemption, not a bar to the requirement.

Para 4.2 requires RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a 48 h recovery at β2=5° and α=20' with salt deposits cleaned off, to be at least the Table 9 value and at most the Table 10 value. The candidate keeps these conditions. It applies to the integrated retro-reflector in the rear lamp. The para 5.1.6 omission option is only a possible exemption.

results.reason: R23 6.1.5 applies to a single lamp that contains more than one light source, and the candidate's wording matches the clause. The spec only says "LED modules on PCB" as the light source for the whole rear lamp. It does not say the reversing lamp has more than one light source, so the candidate's premise is inferred. The number of sources in the reversing lamp is missing.

R23 6.1.6.2 is a conditional failure provision for a single lamp with more than one light source, and the candidate states its options (a) and (b) correctly. The spec does not show that the reversing lamp has multiple independent light sources. Under 6.1.6.1, a group of sources wired so that one failure stops all of them counts as one source, and the spec gives no wiring detail. Applicability therefore cannot be confirmed.

The product has a PMMA retro-reflector, and R150 covers retro-reflectors. Annex 6 Part 6 para 1.1 sets the apparatus requirements for weathering. The candidate keeps them: EN ISO 4892-1 and -2 compliance, temperature and humidity control, and a water spray system.

The clause sets a minimum spray capability of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes for the weathering apparatus used on retro-reflectors. The product includes a retro-reflector, and the candidate matches the clause.
The clause requires the spray water to meet EN ISO 4892-2:2013, as part of the weathering test that applies to the product's retro-reflector. The candidate matches the clause.

The clause allows either a Black-Standard or a Black-Panel thermometer (TM1 or TM2). The candidate states this as a choice between the two, which keeps the clause's meaning. The test applies to the retro-reflector.
The clause requires the test method used to be specified in the report. This follows from the weathering test, which applies to the product's retro-reflector.

The clause requires exposure per EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the Table A6-1 parameters, for 500 hours for retro-reflective devices. The product has a retro-reflector. The 100-hour fluorescent-material case does not apply.

The Table A6-1 values in the candidate match the source: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray cycles, irradiance of 60±2 W/m² and 0.51±0.02 W/m², black-standard 65±3 °C (TM1) or black-panel 63±3 °C (TM2), and relative humidity 50±10 %. The test applies to the retro-reflector.

The clause applies the 70/30 n-heptane and toluol mixture, and para 1.1 names the retro-reflective device as one of the two applicable targets. The product has a retro-reflector. The candidate relies slightly on the sub-paragraph to name the device, but it does not distort the clause.

Para 1.1(a) requires the outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflective device to be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture. This applies to the product's retro-reflector, and the candidate matches the clause.

Para 1.1(b) requires a visual inspection after about five minutes. The surface must show no apparent change, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to. The candidate keeps this exception, and the product has a retro-reflector.

The product has a reversing lamp function, and R23 covers reversing lamps. Paragraph 10.1 lets the approval be withdrawn if lamps bearing the approval mark do not conform to the approved type. The candidate keeps that condition and consequence. It is a little loose in saying "must conform", but this is equivalent in meaning.

Paragraph 11 requires the approval holder to inform the granting authority if it completely ceases to manufacture an approved reversing lamp type. The product includes a reversing lamp, so this applies when the lamp is R23-approved. The candidate keeps the conditions: complete cessation, an approved type, and notice to the authority that granted the approval.

The product is a combined rear lamp that includes a reversing lamp. Clause 4.5.2.1 gives marking on the lamp's light-emitting surface as one option for grouped or combined lamps. The candidate drops the 'or in a group' alternative, but that alternative is covered by candidate 37.
Clause 4.5.2.2 allows marking on the group so that each grouped or combined lamp can be identified. The product is a combined multi-function lamp.
Clause 4.5.3 sets a minimum size for the components of a single approval mark on a combined assembly. The product combines several lamp functions in one housing, so it applies.

Clause 4.5.4 requires an approval number for each approved type and bars the same Contracting Party from reusing it for another grouped or combined lamp type. The candidate matches this, and the product's reversing lamp is part of a combined assembly.

Clause 4.6 requires the mark and symbol to be indelible and clearly legible when the reversing lamp is mounted on the vehicle. The product includes a reversing lamp. The manoeuvring-lamp sub-case does not apply and the candidate omits it.

Section 5 applies the R48 (or R86) general and individual specifications. It applies the requirements pertinent to the lamp and its vehicle category where they can be verified at lamp type approval. The product is an M1 lamp with a reversing function, and the candidate keeps the feasibility condition.
Clause 5.1 says each sample must conform to the specifications that follow. This is general but applies to the reversing lamp in the product.

Clause 5.2 requires reversing lamps to keep working satisfactorily and retain their prescribed characteristics despite vibration in normal use. The product has a reversing lamp function, so this applies directly.

The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers, and its light source is LED modules. Annex 1 item 9 requires the concise description of light source, voltage and wattage, control gear, light source module and installation geometry. The maximum mounting height applies only to manoeuvring lamps, and the candidate's "where applicable" wording keeps that limit.

The reversing lamp function falls under R23, and Annex 1 item 10 requires the communication to state the position of the approval mark. The product evidence is thin, but the obligation matches the clause.
The product includes a reversing lamp. Annex 1 item 11 requires a comment on whether a reversing lamp may be installed only as part of a pair (yes/no), and the candidate states this accurately.
Paragraph 7.3 requires the test voltage to be stated in the communication form. The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers.

Paragraph 7.4 applies to any lamp not fitted with filament lamps. The spec lists LED modules as the light source, so the 1-minute and 10-minute requirements and the 3%/15-minute stability definition apply. The spec does not say outright that the reversing function uses the LEDs, so confidence is a little lower.
Paragraph 7.5 requires the apparent surface of the light-signalling device to be determined in the direction of the reference axis. It applies to the reversing lamp.

Paragraph 8 requires reversing lamp light inside the Annex 3 grid field to be white, with no sharp colour variation outside it. The candidate also keeps the paragraph 7 test reference and the non-replaceable light source exception.
Paragraph 9 requires conformity of production procedures to follow Agreement Appendix 2 plus the R23 requirements. This applies to the approved reversing lamp.
Paragraph 9.1 requires lamps to conform to the approved type, with paragraphs 6 and 8 verified. The candidate matches this.
Paragraph 9.1.1 requires compliance with the Annex 4 minimum conformity of production control requirements. The candidate matches this.
Paragraph 9.1.2 requires compliance with the Annex 5 minimum sampling requirements. The candidate matches this.

Paragraph 9.2 lets the approval authority verify conformity control methods at any time, normally once every two years. The candidate matches this. It is a duty on the manufacturer and authority, but it still applies to the approved reversing lamp.

The product is a single-housing lamp that combines position, stop and reversing functions. The Figure 2 note covers models B, C and D for assemblies of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps. In the note's example, the reversing lamp is shown as AR. The candidate's wording stays within that note.
Annex 3 §1.1 requires stray reflections to be avoided by masking during photometric measurements. The product's reversing lamp falls under R23 photometric testing.

Annex 3 §1.2.1 applies when measurement results are challenged, and the candidate keeps that condition. It requires a measurement distance at which the inverse square law applies. The product has a reversing lamp.

Annex 3 §1.2.2 applies when results are challenged, and the candidate keeps that condition. The receiver must subtend an angle of 10' to 1° from the reference centre. The product has a reversing lamp.

Annex 3 §1.2.3 applies when results are challenged, and the candidate keeps that condition. The intensity requirement is met if the required intensity is obtained within a quarter of a degree of the direction of observation. The product has a reversing lamp.

Annex 3 §2.1 sets H=0°/V=0° as the axis of reference. On the vehicle it is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane and oriented in the required direction of visibility. It passes through the centre of reference. The table gives minimum intensities in cd. This applies to the product's reversing lamp.

The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers. The candidate matches Annex 5 para 3.1: the 20 per cent limit for samples C and D, and the measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by no more than 0 per cent.

It matches Annex 5 para 3.2.1: a deviation over 20 per cent but not over 30 per cent is contested, the manufacturer must align production, a second sampling follows within two months, and samples C and D are retained.
It matches Annex 5 para 3.2.2: a deviation over 30 per cent means the approval is withdrawn and para 5 applies.
It matches Annex 5 para 4: four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment, with the first two marked E and the second two marked F.
It matches Annex 5 para 4.1: the 20 per cent limit for samples E and F, and the measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample E deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
It matches Annex 5 para 4.2: a deviation over 20 per cent in any specimen of E or F is contested, the approval is withdrawn, and para 5 applies.
It matches Annex 5 para 5: approval is withdrawn according to paragraph 10 of R23. This applies to the reversing lamp.

The product includes a reversing lamp, which UN R23 covers. Annex 4 para 2 requires the approval mark holder to run at least the listed tests and to take further samples and restore conformity if a sample fails. The candidate keeps these conditions.
Annex 4 para 2.1 says conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics, and this applies to the product's reversing lamp.
Annex 4 para 2.2.1 says tests are generally carried out by the methods in the Regulation, which applies to the reversing lamp.
Annex 4 para 2.2.2 allows equivalent methods only with the competent authority's consent and puts the burden of proving equivalence on the manufacturer. The candidate preserves both points.
Annex 4 para 2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and its correlation with measurements made by a competent authority. The candidate matches this.
Annex 4 para 2.2.4 makes the Regulation's methods the reference methods, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches this.

Annex 4 para 2.3 requires random sampling from a uniform batch of one type. It also says assessment generally covers individual factories, and records from several factories may be grouped only under the same quality system and management. The candidate preserves these conditions.
Annex 4 para 2.4 requires photometric measurement of the sampled lamp at the Annex 3 minimum-value points and for the required chromaticity coordinates, which applies to the reversing lamp.

Annex 4 para 2.5 requires the manufacturer's statistical study and acceptability criteria agreed with the authority. It sets a 95% confidence level and a minimum 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 5 first-sampling spot check. The candidate matches this.

Paragraph 4.4 is headed "Independent lamps". The product combines several functions in a single housing, so it is a combined or reciprocally incorporated assembly, which paragraph 4.5 covers. Paragraph 4.4 is not the matching route.
Paragraph 4.4.1 sits under the independent-lamps provision. The product is a combined assembly in one housing, so the matching visibility clause is 4.5.1.1.
Paragraph 4.4.2 belongs to the independent-lamps provision (4.4). The product is a combined assembly, so the matching symbol clause is 4.5.2.
Paragraph 4.4.3 applies to independent lamps under 4.4. The product is a combined lamp in a single housing, so this size rule is not shown to apply.
Paragraph 4.4.4 applies to independent lamps under 4.4. The product is a combined assembly in a single housing, which is the 4.5 case.

The rear lamp is a combined assembly with position, stop and reversing functions. Paragraph 4.5 requires each lamp in such an assembly to satisfy this or another Regulation, and the candidate states that correctly.

The product is a combined assembly of lamps. Paragraph 4.5.1 permits a single international approval mark with a circle around E, the country number, an approval number and the arrow if necessary. The candidate keeps the "may" and the visibility and non-removability conditions.
Paragraph 4.5.1.1 requires the single mark on a combined lamp assembly to be visible after installation. The rear lamp is such an assembly.
Paragraph 4.5.1.2 says no light-transmitting part of the combined assembly may be removable without also removing the approval mark. The product has an outer lens that transmits light.

Paragraph 4.5.2 requires an identification symbol for each lamp under each Regulation approved, with the amendment series. The product is a multi-function combined assembly. The candidate leaves out the location options in 4.5.2.1 and 4.5.2.2, which is acceptable.

The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers. Annex 5 1.1 says mechanical and geometric conformity holds if differences stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations. The candidate keeps that meaning.

Annex 5 1.2 sets the photometric conformity test for mass-produced lamps: a randomly chosen lamp is tested per paragraph 7 against the paragraph 6 performance. The candidate keeps this and notes that the criteria are in sub-paragraphs. It applies to the reversing lamp.
Annex 5 1.2.1 requires the Annex 4 paragraph 1.2.1 requirements to be met. The candidate restates this faithfully, and it applies to the reversing lamp's conformity of production.
Annex 5 1.2.3 says lamps with apparent defects are disregarded. The candidate matches this, and the clause applies to sampling of production reversing lamps.
Annex 5 1.3 requires the chromaticity coordinates to comply when tested under paragraph 7. The candidate matches this, and the reversing lamp falls under R23.
Annex 5 section 2 says four lamps are selected at random for the first sampling, as two samples marked A and B. The candidate matches this and applies to production reversing lamps.

Annex 5 2.1 says conformity is not contested if each specimen deviates by no more than 20 per cent. It also says measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent. The candidate keeps both conditions.

Annex 5 2.2 covers the contested case: any specimen deviating by more than 20 per cent, alignment by the manufacturer, repeated sampling within two months, and retention of samples A and B by the Technical Service. The candidate preserves all of these.
Annex 5 section 3 says four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment, marked C and D. The candidate matches this and applies to production reversing lamps.

UN R3 applies to retro-reflectors on M-category vehicles, and the product has one. Clause 3.1 says the applicant is the holder of the trade name or mark, or a duly accredited representative. The candidate drops "if necessary", which does not change the meaning.

Clause 3.1.1 requires triplicate drawings that identify the type, show the fitting positions, and show where the approval number and class indicator go relative to the approval mark circle. The candidate limits the installation-details requirement to Class IB or IIIB. The spec does not give the retro-reflector's class, so that condition is kept as written.
Clause 3.1.2 requires a brief description of the technical specifications of the materials of the retro-reflecting optical unit. The product has a PMMA prism retro-reflector, so the clause applies.

Clause 4.1.1 requires every retro-reflecting device submitted for approval to bear the applicant's trade name or mark. The candidate leaves out the separate conditional "TOP" marking, which is not a problem. The product's retro-reflector is such a device.

results.reason: UN R3 applies to retro-reflecting devices for category M vehicles, and the spec lists a retro-reflector (PMMA prism) in the rear lamp. Annex 10 para 1 requires 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 ±2 °C. The source's "∀" character is a garbled ±. The candidate keeps these conditions.

Annex 10 para 2 requires that, after the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflecting device, and in particular of its optical component, is visible. This applies to the spec's molded PMMA prism retro-reflector. The candidate keeps the source's meaning.

R3 covers retro-reflectors on M-category vehicles, and the product has one. The candidate keeps the clause's condition: it applies only if the unit is a combined optical unit and filter. The spec does not say whether the unit is combined, so the requirement applies only if it is.
The product has a molded PMMA prism retro-reflector, and the clause bans paint or varnish colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters. The candidate restates this accurately.

The retro-reflector is an R3 device, and Annex 6 para 2 sets the colorimetric requirement for reflected light, referring to R48 para 2.30. The candidate restates the illumination conditions accurately.

Annex 7 para 1 requires the applicant to specify the axis or axes of reference when applying for approval. It also requires the photometric measurements to be repeated for each axis, or for the extreme axes of a range. The product's retro-reflector falls under R3, and the candidate keeps these conditions.

Annex 7 para 2 applies to the photometric measurement of the retro-reflector. The candidate keeps the Class IA/IB limits of a 200 mm circle and 100 cm², and the manufacturer's duty to specify the perimeter. The spec does not state the class. Class IA/IB is a reasonable inference for an M1 rear retro-reflector, and the candidate's wording is conditional on that class.

Annex 7 para 3.1.1 sets minimum CIL values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA/IB, and the candidate reproduces the table values and the solid-angle limit. The spec does not state that the retro-reflector is red or give its class. A rear retro-reflector on an M1 car would be red and Class IA/IB, and the candidate's wording is conditional on that.

UN R48 scope covers M and N vehicles for installation of lighting and light-signalling devices. The product is an M1 rear lamp with signalling functions. Paragraph 5.1 requires devices to be fitted so they keep prescribed characteristics despite vibration under normal use, and so the lamps can't be inadvertently maladjusted. The candidate keeps these conditions. It leaves out the cross-reference to the definitions of normal conditions of use, which is acceptable.

The spec lists a retro-reflector (molded PMMA prism optics) in an M1 rear lamp. UN R3 scope covers retro-reflecting devices for category M. Annex 12 para 6 sets the water-penetration verification: one sample A reflector is tested to Annex 8 para 1 (or Annex 14 para 3 for class IVA), and if it fails, both sample B reflectors must pass. The candidate keeps that logic. It omits the sampling reference, which is minor. The quoted product evidence (seal/gasket) is weak, but the retro-reflector itself is in the spec. One caveat: the spec doesn't say the retro-reflector is approved under R3 rather than another regulation.
R3 scope covers retro-reflectors on M-category vehicles, and the product has a retro-reflector. Clause 4.4 requires its markings to be legible and indelible, and the candidate states this faithfully.

Clause 5.1 is an obligation on the approval authority: if all samples meet the requirements, approval shall be granted. The candidate recasts it as 'only if', which the clause does not say. It also sets no design or marking requirement for the product.

The product's retro-reflector falls within R3 as a type-approved device, and clause 5.3 requires an approval number per approved type. The number's first two digits show the series of amendments, and the colour-only extension exception is kept. The duty to assign the number lies with the Contracting Party, so the match is administrative and weaker.

Clause 5.5 requires an approved retro-reflecting device to carry the E-circle with country number, an approval number and the class symbol. These go in the space under 4.2, in addition to the 4.1 markings. The product has a retro-reflector, so the clause applies.

The product is a combined or grouped lamp unit that includes a retro-reflector. Clause 5.6 covers exactly this case: each lamp must satisfy R3 or another Regulation, and a lamp that does not cannot be part of the unit.

Clause 5.6.1 allows a single approval mark on combined lamps that comply with several Regulations, and the candidate keeps that permissive 'may'. Its provisos match sub-clauses 5.6.1.1 and 5.6.1.2, which complete the 'provided that' in 5.6.1. The product is a combined unit with a retro-reflector.
Clause 5.6.1.1 requires the single approval mark on combined lamps to be visible after installation. This applies to the product's combined unit.

Clause 5.6.1.2 says no light-transmitting part of the combined lamps can be removed without also removing the approval mark. The product has a lens and a retro-reflector that transmit light in one unit, so the clause applies.

Clause 5.6.2 requires the identification symbol for each lamp, appropriate to each Regulation under which approval was granted. It also requires the series of amendments. The product combines position, stop and reversing lamps with a retro-reflector, so several Regulations apply.

R48 applies to M and N vehicles. Para 3.2.2 requires the vehicle application to list the lighting and light-signalling devices, each identified by component, approval mark and manufacturer. The M1 rear lamp, with its position, stop and reversing functions, is one of those devices. The obligation sits with the vehicle applicant, and the candidate words it that way.

Para 3.2.4 requires layout drawings for each individual lamp showing the illuminating surface, light-emitting surface, axis of reference and centre of reference. The candidate keeps the 'if necessary' condition. The only exception is the rear registration plate lamp, which this product does not include. The rear lamp's position, stop and reversing functions are individual lamps.

Para 3.2.5 requires a statement of the apparent-surface method, declared for each lamp and recorded in item 10.2 of Annex 1. This applies to the rear lamp's individual lamp functions on an M1 vehicle, and the candidate matches the clause.

The product is a combined rear lamp unit that includes a retro-reflector, so the simplified marking for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (Figure 2, models D/E/F) applies. The note lists the function, Regulation and amendment series for each lamp. The candidate keeps the optional "may" wording. Reading the note as "must identify each function" slightly overreaches.

This sequence is in Annex 4, which covers Class IA and IIIA only. The spec does not state the retro-reflector's class, so applicability can't be confirmed. The candidate text also drops the class condition.

This post-test requirement is in Annex 4, which covers Class IA and IIIA only. The spec does not give the retro-reflector's class, so applicability can't be confirmed. The candidate text also drops the class condition.

Annex 5 para 1.1 requires the illuminating surface of Class IA or IB retro-reflectors not to be easily confused with a triangle. The candidate keeps that class condition. The product is an M1 rear lamp with a retro-reflector, and R3 covers category M. The spec doesn't state the class, but a non-triangular rear reflector (IA or IB) is the plausible case. Paragraph 5.8 requires maximum height to be measured from the highest point and minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. The candidate leaves out the exception that exact edges need not be determined when compliance is clear. That omission does not change the measurement rule.

The candidate keeps this condition by saying it applies only when angles are reduced. The spec does not say whether the product uses reduced visibility angles, but the candidate is conditional, so this does not undermine it.

UN R48 applies to M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp. Paragraph 5.22 says a lamp is deemed not present if it can't operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse, even with an approval mark. The candidate keeps the retro-reflector exception. The spec lists LED modules on PCB as the light source, so the lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) are covered. The spec doesn't say whether the lamp meets this condition, but the candidate states it as a requirement, which matches the clause.

R48 5.8.3 is a general rule for how a lamp's width position is determined. The rear position lamp has width-position requirements, so the rule applies. The candidate keeps the overall-width and inner-edge bases and the exception for cases that clearly comply. The spec gives no width dimensions, so this is only a measurement method.

R48 5.9 is a general rule for any lamp. The product has a stop lamp and other lamps, so it applies. The candidate keeps the "in the absence of specific instructions" condition and the "while switched ON" limit.

R48 5.9.2 allows variation in photometric characteristics for ambient light, other lamps being switched on or off, or use for another function. The variation must comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned. The product combines several light functions, so the clause is relevant and the candidate keeps its conditions.
R48 5.10.1 says red light from a rear-fitted lamp must not be visible from the front. The product is a rear lamp with a red-tinted lens, so it applies. The candidate matches the clause.

Paragraph 5.14.1 prohibits concealing any lamp except main-beam, dipped-beam and front fog lamps. The product is an M1 module with rear position, stop and reversing lamps, and none of these is an excepted lamp. The candidate keeps the exception.

Paragraph 5.15 sets reversing lamp white, stop lamp red, rear position lamp red and rear retro-reflector red (triangular or non-triangular). The product combines all four functions, and the candidate states the colours correctly.

Paragraph 5.16.1 requires the number of lamps on the vehicle to equal the number in the individual specifications. It applies to the M1 vehicle that carries this module, which supplies rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions. The clause sets no specific number, and the product spec gives none, so the requirement is generic.

Clause 2.2.3 requires regular calibration and correlation for the application of both 2.2.1 (the Regulation's own methods) and 2.2.2 (equivalent methods). The candidate limits it to cases where alternative or equivalent methods are used, which narrows the source scope.

Clause 2.2.4 says the reference methods are those of the Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The spec's retro-reflector falls under R3, which covers retro-reflecting devices on M-category vehicles.
Clause 2.3 requires random sampling of retro-reflectors from a uniform batch of the same type. The product has a retro-reflector, so this applies.
Clause 2.4 requires photometric measurements at the specified points and of the chromaticity coordinates on sampled retro-reflectors. The product has a retro-reflector.
Clause 2.5 makes the manufacturer responsible for a statistical study and for defining acceptability criteria in agreement with the competent authority. The wording matches the source.
Clause 2.5 requires criteria giving a minimum probability of 0.95, at a 95 per cent confidence level, of passing an Annex 18 first-sampling spot check. The candidate states this accurately.

Annex 18 para 1.2.1 says conformity is not contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the prescribed minimum values. The candidate matches this and applies to the product's retro-reflector.

Annex 18 para 1.3 says the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with. It applies to retro-reflectors, and the product has one. The cited evidence points to the lens, but the retro-reflector is also in the spec.

Para 2 and 2.2 set out the first sampling: four random retro-reflectors in samples A and B of two each. Conformity is contested if any specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent, and the manufacturer must then align production. The candidate matches this.
Para 3.1 says conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 20 per cent. It applies to the product's retro-reflector.

Para 3.2.1 covers one specimen of C or D above 20 per cent with all at or below 30 per cent. The manufacturer must align again, and a second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification. The candidate matches this.

Para 3.2.2 withdraws approval if a specimen deviates by more than 30 per cent. Para 4.2 withdraws approval if any specimen of E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent, applying para 9 through para 5. The candidate matches this.

R48 5.3 applies to all light-signalling devices on M and N vehicles. The M1 rear lamp qualifies. The candidate keeps the parallel-to-bearing-plane and parallel-to-median-plane conditions, the ±3° tolerance and the manufacturer's fitting instructions.

5.4 sets the verification conditions for lamp height and orientation when there are no specific instructions. It applies to the installed rear lamp. The AFS condition is kept as a conditional.

5.5.1 covers lamps constituting a pair, and rear position and stop lamps on an M1 car are fitted as left/right pairs. The spec does not state this explicitly, so pairing is an inference. The 'absent specific instructions' condition is kept.
