results.reason: Clause 4.2.4 requires the approval marks and symbols to be clearly legible and indelible even when the device is fitted in the vehicle. The rear lamp contains R7 functions (rear position lamp and stop lamp), so it carries these marks. The candidate keeps the clause's wording and conditions.

Clause 4.3.2.1 covers grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that comply with several Regulations. It allows one approval mark, placed anywhere on the lamp if the listed conditions are met. The product combines position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions in one housing, so the clause applies. The spec does not state which other Regulations the lamp is approved under, which is a small gap. The candidate keeps the conditional wording.

Clause 4.3.2.1.1 is a condition on using the single mark on a combined lamp: the mark must be visible after installation. The product is a combined lamp, and the candidate states this condition accurately.

Clause 4.3.2.1.2 is a condition on using the single mark on a combined lamp: no light-transmitting part can be removed without also removing the approval mark. The product has an outer lens and other optical parts in one housing, so the clause applies. The candidate states the condition accurately.

The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp. Both are within UN R7, as definitions 1.2 and 1.3 show. Paragraph 6.6 says Annex 4 gives the measurement methods for light intensity, and the candidate keeps that meaning.

Paragraph 7.1.2 applies only to lamps with non-replaceable light sources. The spec says only "LED modules on PCB" and does not say whether the sources are replaceable. It also does not say whether an electronic control gear or variable intensity control is used, which would bring in 7.1.3 or 7.1.4. The candidate's own reason relies on "most likely", which is an assumption. The spec would need to confirm that the LED sources are non-replaceable.

Clause 4.2.2 is a lead-in to the additional-symbol sub-paragraphs. The product has R7-covered rear position and stop functions, so the general obligation fits. The candidate keeps the condition that symbols apply per covered function. The specific symbols come from the sub-paragraphs.
The product has a rear position lamp. Clause 4.2.2.2 requires the letter R, optionally followed by 1 (steady) or 2 (variable), and the candidate states this accurately.
The product has a stop lamp function. Clause 4.2.2.5 requires S followed by 1, 2, 3 or 4, and the candidate's description of each digit matches the clause.
The spec describes one housing combining a rear position lamp and a stop lamp. Clause 4.2.2.6 requires R, R1 or R2 and S1 or S2, separated by a horizontal dash, and the candidate matches this.

Paragraph 11 of UN R7 applies to a holder of an R7 approval who completely stops making an approved device. The product has rear position and stop lamp functions, which R7 covers. The candidate keeps the condition (complete cessation) and the duty to inform the granting authority. The spec doesn't say whether an approval is held, but the duty only applies to a holder.

Annex 1 of UN R7 sets minimum light-distribution angles for rear position lamps and stop lamps, and the product has both. The candidate gives the 15° above and 15° below default. It also keeps the three exceptions: H plane below 750 mm, optional lamps above 2,100 mm, and S3/S4 stop lamps. It refers the horizontal angles to the Annex 1 diagrams.

The product is a combined rear position and stop lamp, and the reversing lamp and retro-reflector are in the same housing. UN R7 4.3.2.2 requires an identification symbol for each lamp, with the amendment series and the arrow if needed. The candidate keeps those conditions.

4.3.2.2.1 allows the marks on the appropriate light-emitting surface, and 4.3.2.2.2 is the alternative of group marking. The product's outer lens is a light-emitting surface, so the clause applies and the candidate keeps the either/or structure.

4.3.2.2.2 allows group marking so that each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp can be clearly identified. The product groups several lamp functions in one housing, and the candidate matches the clause.

4.3.2.3 sets the minimum size of the components of a single approval mark for grouped or combined lamps. The product is a combined lamp, so it applies when a single mark is used. The candidate restates the clause accurately.

4.3.4 requires the approval marking to be legible and indelible, and visible when fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or door is opened. It applies to the product's lens or housing. The candidate leaves out the permitted placement on an inner or outer part, but that omission does not change the obligation.

Section 5 applies the general and individual specifications of UN R48, or R53, R74 or R86, to each lamp according to the vehicle category. It applies only where verification at lamp type approval is feasible. The product is for an M1 vehicle and contains position and stop lamps, and the candidate keeps the feasibility condition.
5.1 requires each device supplied to conform to paragraphs 6 and 8. The rear position and stop lamp functions fall within UN R7, so the clause applies. The candidate restates it accurately.

The product has rear position and stop lamp functions. Paragraph 6.1 sets minimum and maximum axis intensity, and the rear position row gives 4 to 17 cd for a single lamp. The stop lamp limits are in the separate 6.1.4 rows, but the 6.1 lead-in covers them, so the wording is acceptable.

The product has a rear position lamp, and no variable intensity control is described, so the steady R/R1 category is a reasonable fit. The clause text lists R, R1 or RM1 (steady) and the candidate states no numbers, so it adds no invented values. The spec does not name the lamp's category, which lowers confidence.

The product has a stop lamp. Paragraph 6.1.4 gives S1 (steady) as 60 to 260 cd and S3 (steady) as 25 to 110 cd, and the candidate's examples match. The stop lamp category is not specified in the spec, but the candidate only gives examples by category.

The Annex 3/6 note says the approval number and additional symbols "shall be placed close to the circle" and above, below, right or left of the "E". The candidate states this correctly. The product is a rear lamp that combines a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, which is the device type in Annex 3/6, so the clause applies. The candidate leaves out the other parts of the note, such as digits on the same side and diametrically opposite placement. That is an omission, not a contradiction. Confidence is moderate because the spec does not say the lamp is approved under R7, and the lamp also has reversing and reflector functions, which Annex 3/8 may cover for grouped lamps.
R7 7.4 requires the applied voltage to be noted in the Annex 2 communication form. The product's rear position and stop lamp functions fall under R7 approval, and it is an LED-powered lamp.
R7 7.5 requires the limits of the apparent surface to be determined for a light-signalling device. The rear position and stop lamp functions are covered by R7.

R7 paragraph 8 sets the colour requirement of red or white inside the Annex 4 grid, with no sharp colour variation outside it. It also covers verification with the light sources present for non-replaceable sources. The wording keeps these conditions, and the product's red lens and position and stop functions make it applicable.
R7 paragraph 9 requires conformity of production procedures to follow Agreement Schedule 1. This applies to the approved position and stop lamp functions.
R7 9.1 requires lamps to be manufactured to conform to the approved type, with paragraphs 6 and 8 verified. This applies to the R7 position and stop lamp functions.
R7 9.1.1 requires compliance with the Annex 5 minimum conformity of production control requirements. This applies to the approved lamp.
R7 9.1.2 requires compliance with the Annex 6 minimum sampling requirements. This applies to production lamps of the approved type.

The text of R7 9.2 is in the same clause. It says the approving authority may at any time verify conformity control methods at each production facility, normally once every two years. This is an authority action that affects the product's manufacturer, and the candidate preserves it.

R7 10.1 allows approval to be withdrawn if the conformity conditions are not met. The candidate's statement that the lamp must keep meeting them is a reasonable consequence for the approved position and stop lamp.

The deeming rule is conditional, and the candidate keeps that condition. The spec lists 'LED modules on PCB' (plural) in a lamp with several light functions, so it plausibly has more than one source. The wiring is not stated, so applicability is only probable.

Clause 6.1.7.2 sets the failure-mode options: either the Annex 4 minimum intensity is still met, or a tell-tale is used. The tell-tale option needs at least 50% of the minimum intensity on the reference axis and a note in the communication form. The candidate keeps these conditions. The plural LED modules suggest a multi-source lamp, though this is not confirmed.
Clause 6.2.1 requires intensity in each Annex 4 direction to be at least the 6.1 minimum times the table percentage. The product has rear position and stop lamp functions that this covers.
Clause 6.2.2 caps intensity at the 6.1 maximum in any direction from which the device is visible. It applies to the position and stop lamp functions of the product.

Clause 6.2.4.1 sets a minimum of 0.05 cd for rear position lamps throughout the Annex 1 fields. The candidate correctly limits the 0.3 cd and 0.07 cd values to S-category devices. The product has a rear position lamp.
Clause 6.2.4.3 requires the Annex 4 paragraph 2.2 local-variation provisions to be observed. The candidate matches this, and it applies to the product's position and stop lamp light distribution.

Clause 6.3 requires intensities to be measured with the sources continuously alight, and in coloured light for red-emitting devices. The product has a red-tinted lens, so the red-light condition applies.

The rear lamp combines rear position, stop and reversing lamps and a retro-reflector in one housing. That is a grouped or combined assembly, so Annex 3 section 8 (simplified marking) is relevant. The permissive wording ("may use") matches the source's illustrative models.
Annex 4 1.1 applies to photometric measurements of R7 lamps. The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, and the candidate wording matches the clause.
Annex 4 1.2.1 applies to R7 photometry of the product's rear position and stop lamps. The candidate keeps the condition from the parent clause 1.2 ("when measurements are challenged").

Annex 4 1.2.2 applies to photometry of the product's stop and rear position lamps. The candidate keeps the challenged-measurement condition from clause 1.2 and the 10 minute to 1 degree aperture range.

Annex 4 1.2.3 sits under clause 1.2, which applies only "in case the results of measurements should be challenged". The candidate states the quarter-degree tolerance as a general rule and drops that condition. Candidates 188 and 189 keep it.

The product includes a rear position lamp and a stop lamp. Both are defined in UN R7 (1.2 and 1.3), so the regulation applies to those functions. Annex 6 / 5 says approval is withdrawn according to paragraph 10. The trigger comes from the adjacent clause 4.2, which says approval is withdrawn when a sampled lamp deviates by more than 20 per cent, and then refers to paragraph 5. The candidate states that trigger generally as "do not conform" and does not add a separate obligation. It limits the consequence to the position and stop lamps, so the reversing lamp is not wrongly pulled in. I did not read paragraph 10 itself.

UN R7 covers rear position lamps and stop lamps. The product has both, so R7 applies. Annex 2 item 9.1 asks for a concise description by lamp category. That description includes colour, number, category and kind of light source, voltage and wattage, mounting height, installation geometry, control gear or variable intensity, and the tell-tale condition. The candidate reflects these items without adding obligations. It leaves out the light source module identification code, which is a minor omission. The spec confirms LED light sources and red rear and stop functions. It gives no values for the fields, and the candidate does not invent any. The reversing lamp and retro-reflector fall under other regulations, but they do not affect this match.

UN R7 covers rear position and stop lamps, and the product has both. Annex 5 1.2 sets the conformity-of-production photometric criterion, and the candidate keeps its meaning. The clause only introduces the criteria that follow, and the candidate says so.

The 20% maximum unfavourable deviation and the 0.3 cd and 0.05 cd table values match Annex 5 1.2.1. The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, so the clause applies. The candidate leaves out the 30% column, which does not change the 20% obligation.
Annex 5 1.3 requires colorimetric performance to comply with paragraph 8. The product's red outer lens defines the lamp colour, so the clause applies.

Annex 5 2 requires the approval-mark holder to run the tests at appropriate intervals, take further samples on non-conformity, and act to ensure production conformity. The candidate matches this, and it applies to the product's stop and position lamps.
Annex 5 2.1 says conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics. It applies to the product's R7 lamp functions.
Annex 5 2.2.1 says tests are generally carried out by the methods in the Regulation. The candidate matches it and the product's R7 lamps are within scope.

Annex 5 2.2.2 allows equivalent methods only with the competent authority's consent, and the manufacturer must prove equivalence. The candidate keeps this condition. It applies when the manufacturer uses equivalent methods for the product's R7 lamps.
The product has rear position and stop lamps, which R7 covers. Annex 6 para 1.3 requires the chromaticity coordinates to comply when tested under para 7, and the candidate keeps that condition.
Annex 6 para 2 selects four lamps at random and splits them into samples A and B of two lamps each. The candidate matches this, and the product's rear position and stop lamps are R7 devices.

Para 2.1 says conformity is not contested if no specimen of A and B deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent. The candidate matches.
Para 2.2 covers contested conformity, the request to bring production into line, repeated sampling within two months of notification, and retention of samples A and B. The candidate matches.
Para 3 selects four lamps at random from stock made after alignment and splits them into samples C and D. The candidate matches.

Para 3.1 matches the candidate. Conformity is not contested if no specimen of C and D deviates by more than 20 per cent, and measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
